import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Region': ['North America', 'North America', 'North America', 'North America', 'North America', 'North America',
               'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa',
               'United States', 'United States', 'United States', 'United States', 'United States', 'United States',
               'Western Europe', 'Western Europe', 'Western Europe', 'Western Europe', 'Western Europe', 'Western Europe',
               'East Asia & Pacific', 'East Asia & Pacific', 'East Asia & Pacific', 'East Asia & Pacific', 'East Asia & Pacific', 'East Asia & Pacific',
               'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia'],
    'Year': [1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995,
             1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995,
             1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995,
             1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995,
             1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995,
             1970, 1975, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1995],
    'Urbanization Rate (%)': [40.1, 42.5, 45.8, 48.2, 51.3, 53.7,
                              35.2, 39.1, 42.7, 46.0, 49.1, 51.8,
                              42.5, 45.3, 48.7, 51.2, 53.8, 56.1,
                              68.5, 70.6, 72.9, 74.7, 76.2, 77.5,
                              31.0, 35.5, 39.8, 43.2, 46.7, 49.5,
                              21.2, 23.5, 26.1, 28.8, 31.6, 34.3],
    'Population Growth (%)': [0.8, 1.2, 1.1, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5,
                              1.5, 1.7, 1.3, 1.1, 0.9, 0.8,
                              0.7, 0.9, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4,
                              0.9, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2,
                              1.1, 1.3, 1.2, 0.9, 0.7, 0.6,
                              1.5, 1.8, 1.6, 1.2, 1.0, 0.9]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd', '#8c564b']

for i, region in enumerate(df['Region'].unique()):
    region_data = df[df['Region'] == region]
    plt.plot(region_data['Year'], region_data['Population Growth (%)'],
             marker='o', label=region, color=colors[i], linewidth=2.5)

plt.title('Population Growth Trends by Region (1970-1995)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Urbanization Rate (%)', fontsize=12)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.legend(title='Region', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.xticks(df['Year'].unique())
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png')

The image is a line chart titled "Urbanization Rate Trends by Region (1970-1995)," which illustrates how urbanization rates have evolved across six different regions over a 25-year period. The x-axis represents the years, ranging from 1970 to 1995 in five-year increments, while the y-axis shows the urbanization rate as a percentage, spanning from 20% to 80%.

Each region is represented by a distinct colored line with circular markers at each data point. Western Europe, depicted in red, consistently exhibits the highest urbanization rates throughout the period, starting at 68.5% in 1970 and rising steadily to 77.5% by 1995. The United States, shown in green, also maintains high urbanization rates, beginning at 42.5% in 1970 and increasing to 56.1% by 1995. North America, displayed in blue, starts at 40.1% in 1970 and grows to 53.7% by 1995, showing a gradual upward trend.

The Middle East & North Africa, represented in orange, starts at a lower urbanization rate of 35.2% in 1970 and climbs to 51.8% by 1995, showing significant growth over the period. East Asia & Pacific, shown in purple, begins at 31.0% in 1970 and rises to 49.5% by 1995, reflecting a notable increase. South Asia, depicted in brown, has the lowest urbanization rates among the regions, starting at 21.2% in 1970 and increasing to 34.3% by 1995, though its growth trajectory remains steady and consistent.

The chart features a clean grid with dashed lines for better readability and includes a legend positioned outside the plot area to the right, clearly identifying each region by color. The overall trend across all regions indicates a general increase in urbanization rates over the 25-year span.
